title: AI model evaluation
_contract: This file RENAMES and CONTEXTUALISES. It must never assert a cause the engine cannot distinguish. Every check below carries `consistent_with`, `but_also` and `distinguish_by` rather than a verdict, because `basis_conflicts` reports that a pair's correlation rose after a transform and CANNOT tell whether a factor was injected (a defect) or a real duplicate exposed (a finding). Both were observed on one corpus: ROA~ROE 0.60 to 0.98 was injected; NETINC~ROA 0.06 to 0.9997 was real. Same signature. A lexicon entry that prints one reading as fact makes the tool claim what the engine explicitly refuses to.
_denominator_note: Candidates only. The engine never infers a denominator; the operator declares one with --scale-by. Listed here so the operator knows what is usually worth declaring in this domain.
_exempt_note: Suggested --scale-exempt. These are already rates or bounded scores. Dividing them by a size INJECTS a size factor — measured on bank data, dividing two rates by total assets took their correlation from +0.60 to +0.98 and pushed them past the clustering threshold. Suggestion, not a default: the operator declares.

basis-conflict.label: Score moves with output length
basis-conflict.consistent_with: verbosity effects — a grader rewarding length, so the score tracks how much was written rather than how well.
basis-conflict.but_also: a real relationship — longer chains genuinely solving harder problems better. Nothing in the arithmetic separates these.
basis-conflict.distinguish_by: hold length roughly fixed and see whether the score still separates models; or grade a length-matched subset. If the score survives length-matching, it is measuring reasoning.
basis-conflict._status: UNVALIDATED — no corpus with output-length data has been run. Treat as a hypothesis to check, not a finding this tool has ever made.

identity.label: Two evals reporting one number
identity.consistent_with: the same benchmark under two names, or a metric and its own rescaling.
identity.but_also: two genuinely different evals that happen to rank models identically on this sample.
identity.distinguish_by: check whether they diverge on any model in the set. If none does, one of them is free.
identity._status: Validated: three benchmarks appeared twice on one leaderboard at r = 1.0000 (Raw and normalised).

subset-sum.label: Composite score is its parts added up
subset-sum.consistent_with: an aggregate leaderboard column carrying no information its components lack.
subset-sum.but_also: nothing — this one is arithmetic. The relation holds on at least 99% of rows or it is not reported.
subset-sum.distinguish_by: not needed. Archive the composite, keep the parts; the composite is recomputable and the parts are not.

trend-confound.label: Everything improved together
trend-confound.consistent_with: a shared driver — a base-model upgrade, a prompt change, a grader revision — lifting every eval at once.
trend-confound.distinguish_by: the differenced basis. If the correlation survives differencing, it is not just the shared timeline.

_validation: Scored against 541 models from the HuggingFace Open LLM Leaderboard on 02/08/2026 — see AI_EVAL_PREREG.md. VALIDATED: heavy redundancy (15 columns to 2.24 effective signals), duplicate benchmarks as exact identities, nonlinear coupling between scores and model size. NOT VALIDATED: the basis-conflict entry. That corpus carries no token-count or response-length column, so the verbosity reading has never been tested against data. Five other predictions holding does not license it.
